title: Detection and Inhibition of Decoherence Through Collisions: A dynamical approach
authors: Sagnik Chakraborty, Srijon Ghosh, Federico Amato, Gniewomir Sarbicki, Dariusz Chruściński, Rosario Lo Franco
abstract: Quantum systems are intrinsically fragile and highly vulnerable to environmental noise, making the preservation of quantum states one of the fundamental challenges in realizing practical quantum technologies. We propose two noise-agnostic quantum state protection protocols based on a collisional model. The first protocol preserves quantum states of qubits without requiring complete prior knowledge of the underlying noise dynamics, and the second even protects a logical qubit under similar circumstances. These protocols provide robust protection for arbitrary single-qubit and entangled states against general noise processes. Furthermore, their capability to safeguard quantum states with an arbitrary number of qubits enhances the reliability, robustness, and scalability of emerging quantum architectures. These results establish the proposed framework as a promising approach for practical quantum information processing.
summary: This paper introduces a novel, noise-agnostic quantum state protection protocol based on collisional dynamics. It details a detection-and-recovery cycle that allows quantum systems to actively counteract environmental noise without needing full knowledge of the noise process. The framework successfully demonstrates high-fidelity state preservation for single, entangled, and logical qubits.
main_problem: The core challenge is preserving fragile quantum states against environmental noise (decoherence) to enable practical quantum technologies.
main_result: The proposed collisional model protocol provides robust, noise-agnostic protection for arbitrary single-qubit, entangled, and logical quantum states.
method: The protocol uses a detection-and-recovery cycle involving collisions with ancillas, minimum-error discrimination measurements to diagnose noise, and applying the Petz recovery map.
model_or_system: The system involves quantum states (single-qubit, multi-qubit, logical subspaces) interacting with an environment, modeled using a collisional model (CM) framework.
key_observables: Fidelity (F), which measures state preservation; Infidelity (1-F), which measures deviation from the initial state.
important_parameters: Noise strengths ($\gamma_1, \gamma_2$), time evolution ($\Delta t$), and the number of qubits ($N$).
main_assumptions: The protocol assumes the ability to perform optimal discrimination measurements on the ancilla and that the Petz recovery map can be effectively implemented via collision dynamics.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the protocol schematic, showing steps for single and multiple runs, and plot fidelity vs. noise actions, comparing recovered evolution against free evolution.
paper_structure: The paper develops the protocol by first outlining the general collisional model, detailing the iterative steps of detection and recovery, and then applying this framework to single-qubit, multi-qubit, and logical subspace protection.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses open quantum systems dynamics and quantum error correction, providing a concrete, implementable framework for mitigating decoherence using measurement-based feedback.
